paragraphs: On Wednesday afternoon, Teacher Kim's class plays "Who Am I?" Each child writes a riddle card about a person or a creature. A classmate reads the card and guesses the answer. The children listen. The answer is on the back of the card, with a picture. "You are a clever class," says Teacher Kim. "Please say, 'It may be ...' when you guess."

Leo's card says, "I have two wings and a big beak. I live in a nest. Who am I?" Mia says, "It may be an eagle." Leo smiles and nods. Mia's card says, "I wear a uniform and fly a big plane." Leo says, "It may be a pilot." May's card says, "I sing songs on a stage, and I wear a red dress." Lily says, "It may be a singer."

Leo's next card says, "I am big and brown. I live in the zoo. I have a hump, and I like the hot desert." May says, "It may be a camel." Mia's next card says, "I am white. I have a long neck, and I swim on a lake." Leo says, "It may be a swan." Mia smiles. May's next card says, "I am very small. I have six legs, and I live in the garden." "It may be an insect," says Lily.

Teacher Kim writes three short cards for the class. The first says, "I paint pictures." The next says, "I bring food to your table." The last says, "I put out fires." "They may be an artist, a waiter, and a fire fighter," says Mia. Last, Lily's card says, "I am small and brown. I have soft fur and a red collar." The class says, "It may be Pip!" Lily smiles and turns the card. There is a picture of a puppy. Teacher Kim claps. She asks, "Who has the next card?" She gives each card a small star.
